newsitem.title: USA: Payless gets court approval for financing.
newsitem.headline: Payless gets court approval for financing.

text.p: Payless Cashways Inc, which filed for bankruptcy protection earlier Monday, said it received court approval of interim debtor-in-possession financing provided under a loan agreement with a group of banks.

On an interim basis, the court approved $90 million of the $125 million DIP financing intended to provide funding for all post-petition trade and employee obligations as well as the company's ongoing operating needs during the restructuring process, Payless said in a statement.
The court scheduled a final hearing for the remaining $35 million of the DIP financing for August 20.

"We are pleased that the court promptly approved the company's request for financing," David Stanley, chairman and chief executive officer, said in the statement. "This funding will help provide our vendors with additional financial assurances that we will be operating on a business-as-usual basis."

In hearings today, the court approved the company's request to pay pre-petition employee wages and benefits, and to use cash and existing bank accounts to pay pre-petition claims of independent contractors.

Earlier today, Payless filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Missouri in Kansas City a voluntary petition to reorganize under Chapter 11 of the bankruptcy code and a plan of reorganization for its emergence from bankruptcy.
Payless operates 194 building materials stores in 22 states.
